label: input h/x/e after x/o/n/v/e (weak token-bigram tendency)
explanation: Sparse (about 1% of steps). Most strongly tied to the current input token: h (9.4x lift, 33% of activation mass), x and e (about 5x each), and boosted when the previous token is x/o/n/v/e. It never fires at t=0 and is enriched at early original positions (t=1-3) and at the first copy step after the delimiter (recall_idx=1). The top activations are mostly h input right after <DEL> or early in the sequence. Even so, only 5-9% of h/x/e inputs activate it, and the best bigram predicate reaches dev F1 0.31 (precision 0.27, mass recall 0.44). The rest of the activation mass is spread over many other token contexts. It looks like a distributed hash of the token history rather than a nameable feature. It is almost silent on the delimiter step itself.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=1: h, e, x, v; t=4: h, x, e, n; t=3: h, e, x, n) and the previous input (most: x, n, o, v, e, m; least: p, y, -, q); timing cues that raise it most: L=8 & t=9, L=3 & t=1, L=6 & t=5.
